page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.gn6i-c24g1.12xlarge is a GPU-accelerated compute instance powered by the KVM hypervisor and x86_64 architecture. The system provides 48 dedicated virtual CPUs derived from 24 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8163 processor clocked at 2.5 GHz, supported by 33 MB of L3 cache. Memory capacity totals 186.0 GB, which yields roughly 3.88 GB of RAM per vCPU. Hardware acceleration is provided by two bundled NVIDIA Turing T4 GPUs delivering a combined 32 GB of VRAM. There is no bundled local storage, requiring network-attached storage for persistent disks. Baseline networking throughput is rated at 15 Gbps.

Benchmark results demonstrate solid parallel scaling alongside moderate single-thread compute capabilities. In stress-ng testing, single-core execution scored 1104.08, placing it in the bottom 25%, while multi-core execution reached 35393.62, falling within the middle 50%. Decompression via bzip3 scaled from 7.62 GB/sec single-threaded to 149.01 GB/sec across all available threads. Memory subsystems produced uncached sequential read speeds of 98.26 GB/sec and write speeds of 44.08 GB/sec. Application testing showed balanced throughput, handling 33.17 million Redis SET operations per second and 22.34 GB/sec in static web serving benchmarks.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the instance balances 48 host vCPUs against dual entry-level inference accelerators. The pairing avoids the heavy capital allocation required by high-end training silicon while delivering dedicated GPU access for parallelized operations. The primary engineering tradeoff stems from modest single-threaded CPU speed and the lack of local scratch disks, which limits suitability for disk-bound IOPS operations without network block storage. This instance type aligns with machine learning inference, distributed video transcoding, computer vision pipeline processing, and multi-threaded analytical services.
